actions.action: Move the plant back from the sunny window glass
Check the soil 2-3 inches down to see whether it stays wet
Check the stems at soil level for softness or a bad smell
Check whether the pot has a drainage hole or water pools in the base
Inspect the leaf undersides for spider mites or thrips
If the pot has no hole, repot into a pot with drainage
Alternatively, use a cache pot and take the plant out to water
Place the plant in bright indirect light away from direct afternoon sun
Relocate the plant away from drafts, heaters and AC vents
Remove the leaf once it is mostly yellow or brown
Watch new growth over the next few weeks

reason: The answer favors move or light stress over overwatering and only lists overwatering and drainage as a secondary possibility, so the drainage and dry-out fix is present but not central; its reassurance about watering is tempered by soil checks, so it is not harmful.
